title: BBS: Bi-Directional Bit-Level Sparsity for Deep Learning Acceleration
problem: Existing accelerators exploit sparsity at coarse granularities (structured, vector-level) and typically in only one dimension (weights or activations), missing fine-grained optimization opportunities. Bit-level sparsity remains largely unexploited, especially in bidirectional fashion.
motivation: Bit-level sparsity in both weights and activations can deliver significant throughput and energy efficiency gains by skipping zero-bit operations.
method: BBS implements bidirectional bit-level sparsity detection and exploitation in hardware, identifying zero bits in both weight and activation streams and routing computations only to non-zero positions. The architecture uses efficient masking and skipping mechanisms with dedicated bit-level granularity support and control logic to minimize overhead while maximizing the benefits of sparse bit patterns.
key_novelty: First to exploit bit-level sparsity simultaneously and bidirectionally across both weights and activations in a hardware accelerator design.
contributions: Bidirectional bit-level sparsity exploitation framework spanning both weight and activation dimensions
Hardware-efficient detection and skip mechanisms for zero-bit operations with low control overhead
Specialized accelerator architecture supporting fine-grained bit-level sparsity
Comprehensive evaluation across CNN and transformer workloads demonstrating performance and energy gains

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: improved energy efficiency through reduced bit operations

primary_theme: Bidirectional bit-level sparsity for DNN acceleration
